name: City View - Sarah's double room.
description: A good sized room with a comfy double bed and views across Bristol. Wander to the local park in the morning, pop to the harbourside to explore for the day and head to the local in the evening!
neighborhood_overview:
The neighbourhood is friendly and welcoming; most houses are Victorian like mine, but the ones opposite are old miners cottages from the 1860's.

Much of community life centres around Victoria Park which is a large lovely green space at the end of my road. It has a children's play area, a lovely little café that you can dash to for bacon sarnies in the morning and great views across Bristol.

There is a city farm a few minutes walk away as well and a meander into the centre of Bristol takes you through the park and you can choose to go easily along the harbourside to see the best of beautiful Bristol.
host_about: I am pretty laid back, enjoy meeting new people and having my house lived in by anyone who comes to stay, love being out in the wilds with a tent or out walking, swing dance fanatic, and nearly always have a good Malbec open. Love a good unicorn! I work in the charity and childcare sector.

description: A small double room in an artist's house, with North Street indy culture, bars and shops on the doorstep. Nestled on a quiet street just next to the action. Enjoy breakfast in the garden. 17 minutes' walk from the centre of Bristol / 2 minutes from the bus stop.
neighborhood_overview:

Huge murals and street art cover most buildings, thanks to the annual Street Art festival, Upfest. The Tobacco Factory Theatre hosts plays, comedy, classes and a great weekly market. Tom and I speak some Spanish and have mostly forgotten how to speak French, German and Japanese, but can stumble through a conversation if prompted :)

description: Close to Bristol and Bath Railway Path, leading to Bath and Bristol City Centre: Bike, walk or bus ride. Local train station connects to Bristol Temple Mead Station & elsewhere. Excellent grocery stores, great cafes & eateries, friendly pubs. Set in a quiet residential backwater, close to parks & green walking spaces with quick and easy access to the city. I like walking, nature and yoga.

description:

You have a minifridge, kettle and microwave in your room. The main kitchen is out of use for guests due to my food allergies.

We have easy access by car (on-street parking only) & bus. Breakfast isn't provided as we're next to Sainsbury's.

neighborhood_overview:

Sandy Park Road is the main street 2 minutes away with a deli, Post Office, charity shops, coffee shops, bike shop, bakers, Chinese takeway, fish and chips, launderette, dry cleaners etc.

Arnos Vale park and Arnos Vale cemetery are at the end of the road and a lovely place to stroll.

We're not far from the Paintworks and the excellent Bocabar for pizzas and more, and the Bristol Eats.

There's a cinema a couple of minutes walk away, as well as other shops including M&S Food, Boots, The Range, Wilko, Iceland. and every kind of fast food outlet (Costa Coffee, Greggs, Krispy Kreme, McDonalds, Kentucky, Burger King) you might require.
host_about:

I'm in my mid 50s and have done the partying so now am an early to bed, early to rise person and  love going to bed early with a good book  I always aim for 8 hours sleep. I try to fit in gym classes daily, and  meditate regularly.

I like to keep a clean and tidy home (and hope if you're staying with me you would respect that and keep it clean/ check my house rules).

name: Tranquil Room near City Centre
host_about:
My name is Joanne. I am from New Zealand and have been living in the UK for over thirty years, living in London for 15 years before settling here in Bristol for twenty years now. 

In 2013  I joined the Airbnb Community offering homestay accommodation to travellers & visitors, university students, those looking to relocate and or work in Bristol for short stay visits. 

My previous experience of homestay hosting involved working closely with an established Bristol English Language School, 2010 -2013. I was valued by them for my contribution to homestay experiences offered to their foreign language students. 

With the unprecedented events of the 2020 Covid 19 Pandemic, I closed my doors to hosting from March 2020 until  
June 2021. The three lockdown phases, in particular, though challenging at times, offered me & I hope others some extraordinary experiences, a time to pause, reflect, restore, regroup. So much to fathom during them & in the uncertain times we now continue to face. Gentle, gentle. 

It was with some reticence I concede, that I opened my doors to hosting again in the last weeks of June 2021. I am rediscovering again the enriching experience of sharing my home, creating a welcoming, relaxed & comfortable experience for others, a space where connecting in good conversation is valued & respected as much as the need for privacy & discretion. 

I feel immense gratitude for the experiences I have shared & been privilege to with guests through Airbnb hosting & I look forward to the many more experiences to come my way. 
With much warmth & appreciation, Joanne

My name is Joanne. I am from New Zealand and have been living in the UK for over thirty years, living in London for 15 years before settling here in Bristol for twenty years now. 

In 2013  I joined the Airbnb Community offering homestay accommodation to travellers & visitors, university students, those looking to relocate and or work in Bristol for short stay visits. 

My previous experience of homestay hosting involved working closely with an established Bristol English Language School, 2010 -2013. I was valued by them for my contribution to homestay experiences offered to their foreign language students. 

With the unprecedented events of the 2020 Covid 19 Pandemic, I closed my doors to hosting from March 2020 until  
June 2021. The three lockdown phases, in particular, though challenging at times, offered me & I hope others some extraordinary experiences, a time to pause, reflect, restore, regroup. So much to fathom during them & in the uncertain times we now continue to face. Gentle, gentle. 

It was with some reticence I concede, that I opened my doors to hosting again in the last weeks of June 2021. I am rediscovering again the enriching experience of sharing my home, creating a welcoming, relaxed & comfortable experience for others, a space where connecting in good conversation is valued & respected as much as the need for privacy & discretion. 

I feel immense gratitude for the experiences I have shared & been privilege to with guests through Airbnb hosting & I look forward to the many more experiences to come my way. 
With much warmth & appreciation, Joanne

Although Tudor House is located in a quiet neighbourhood in leafy Redland, just around the corner on  Whiteladie's Road is great nightlife with restaurants, bars and pubs. The  immediate environment is friendly and quiet with small shops and local pubs but the city centre is close by.
neighborhood_overview: Redland together with Clifton are probably the nicest parts of Bristol to live in. With its tree lined streets, parks and large Victorian and Georgian houses it has a wonderful character. However it still is close to all the amenities you may need and sights you will want to see whilst visiting. Just around the corner from the flat on Whiteladies Road are number of friendly restaurants, such as the Boston Tea Party, The Townhouse or the Cowshed  with good breakfast, lunch and dinner menus. There are many more restaurants and pubs just around the corner on Cotham Hill, but the immediate environment of the flat is quiet and homely. My particular favourites are the Highbury Vaults pub on St Michael's Hill, just up the Cotham Hill and to the right, The Lido restaurant close by in Clifton (open) and the River Cottage Restaurant on Whiteladies Road (closed at the moment). Clifton Down Shopping Centre is within 5 minutes walking distance with a Sainsbury's supermarket, Pharmacy and other  use
host_about: I love Art, travel, good food,people and my work as a designer architect... For my leisure I keep fit swimming and gymming, I love sailing, skiing when I can find the time and try to enjoy life as much as possible in hopefully healthy way. When travelling I prefer to do it not as a tourist but try to imagine what it is like to live in the place... I have lived in Prague, London, Hong Kong, Dubai and for the past 12 years in Shanghai... and travelled extensively in Europe, US, Middle East, Asia and SE Asia. I have stayed in apartments through Airbnb  and have had a great experience of the city this way. My permanent home is Bristol, the city I always love to return to from my travels.

neighborhood_overview: Montpelier is an extremely colourful, laid back, foodie neighbourhood in the centre of Bristol.  With so much on our doorstep in terms of restaurants, cafes, green parks, music, late night clubs, and general... fun!
host_about:
Hi! I've been living in Bristol, on and off, for 13 years and still absolutely love it here.  Our house is down a quiet dead-end street in Montpelier, but only about 50 metres from the chaos and brilliance of Stokes Croft.  We're massively spoilt to be so close to such great music venues, pubs, galleries, fabulous cafes and restaurants and generally just so much exciting, inspiring energy!  

I used to love Bristol for it's incredible freedom and decedent party culture, and now, since having children, I love it even more for it's brilliant parks, museums, community centres and easy proximity to fields, forests and water.  

I feel really happy to share our home with others through airbnb and hope that the space and location will inspire lots of fun, warmth and comfort for those who stay here. description: This beautifully presented one bedroom ground floor flat is perfectly located by the popular Whiteladies Road area of Clifton with its abundance of cafes, restaurants, bars and shops all within walking distance.
neighborhood_overview: The location is fantastic and is a 30-second walk from the bars and restaurants and bus stops on Whiteladies Road. host_about:
Hi, I’m Andie and have lived in Bristol for 7.5 years.  I moved from London in 2010 and have never looked back!  It’s such a fantastic, diverse city with so much going on.  The food, bar and music scene is incredible and, in my opinion, rivals London, yet it is relatively inexpensive.

I have lived in my beautiful flat for 6.5 years and restored it myself in my spare time.  I hope you enjoy it as much as I do.  It is on the reception floor of a Victorian home, so it has the most grand reception room in the building with the traditional features of original shutters, cornicing and huge marble fireplace, ceiling rose, and deep skirting boards.  Please understand that the building is >150 years old so it has its quirks and it is not well sound-proofed.  My neighbours (upstairs and downstairs) are very friendly and I’m sure they’ll welcome you.

I am away on a short-term basis so it still very much looks like a home, albeit a bit less cluttered!  I hope you find it a good home-from-home during your stay in Bristol.

The location is fantastic and is a 30-second walk from the bars and restaurants on Whiteladies Road.  It is also central to Clifton, Gloucester/Cheltenham Road and the city centre/shopping district.  I walk everywhere from my flat and you can be at all these places in an easy 20 minute walk in either direction.  Equally, if you fancy getting out of town to the local countryside or nearby cities like Bath and Cheltenham, this is remarkably easy and quick (just try not to travel in rush hour!).

My favourite place to eat in Bristol is the superb tapas bar called Bravas, which is literally at the end of my road and it is always an easy stumble home after one too many dishes of patatas bravas!  I can thoroughly recommend the Iberico pork and deep fried aubergine in molasses.  Trust me!  I recommend booking as it’s a small place and very popular.

There’s a quirky bar called HMSS (Her Majesty’s Secret Service) right next to Clifton Down Shopping Centre, within a few minutes’ walk.  It does fantastic cocktails that are elaborately and imaginatively served.

There’s also a fantastic brunch spot at the end of my road (corner of Hampton Park and Cotham Hill) called Rubicon Too and they have seating outside, which is a wonderful sun-trap on a sunny morning, but equally lovely on a colder weekend day.  The pub opposite the cafe, The Brewhouse, has a lovely outside seating area (opposite Rubicon Too), which is very popular in the summer.  It is one of the few spots in Bristol where you can bask in the sun whilst nursing a glass of wine or cold beer.

There are all sorts of wonderful attractions in the city centre, also walking distance or a short bus ride.  The bus stop is about a minutes’ walk away, as is Clifton Down shopping centre with all the local amenities you could need, including a large supermarket (Sainsburys), pharmacy (Boots) and stationers (WH Smith).

Clifton Suspension Bridge is c25 minute walk away, or a quick taxi ride, and Brunel’s SS Great Britain is also relatively close, on the south side of the river.  There are various Banksy murals dotted around Bristol too.

If you’re in Bristol for work, my flat is a few minutes’ walk from the BBC, about 15-20 minutes from Bristol Royal Infirmary (main hospital) and c10 minutes from the university (city centre campus).

I hope you enjoy your stay in Bristol, and my flat, as much as I do.

Best wishes,
Andie.

neighborhood_overview:
History
The Exchange dates back to the mid-18th century. However, it wasn’t until 1869, after nearly 30 years of housing a bi-weekly corn market, that the structure gained its now famous glass roof. Although the roof itself was replaced shortly after the Second World War, St Nicks holds onto much of its vintage charm. It is the last 18-century exchange building of its kind in the city. Nowadays, the market atmosphere remains, yet the Glass Arcade is now home to numerous independent food purveyors, eager to serve up culinary delights with a smile and a warm welcome.

The Market Today
There are plenty of different stalls to sample, but rest assured that you can’t go wrong with any of them. The team of traders cater for a variety of needs, be it lunch to go or more of a sit-down affair. The stalls themselves are famous in the city, for both the variety of their produce and the sheer deliciousness of what they’ve got to offer.

Cosy Tree house with lovely lake views nestled in the corner of our garden. This space has it's own private balcony, a hot outdoor shower and compost toilet. We are doing our bit to help save the planet.
You can enjoy a night under the stars with the raised bed. This means there is a ladder to climb! So please consider this when booking.
Snuggle up, get cosy and play some games or read a book on the sofa in the day. We aren’t far from the vibrant centre of Bristol or the quirkier areas too.
neighborhood_overview: We live in one of the safest streets in Bristol with friendly neighbours and plenty of FREE on street parking. We're just round the corner from IKEA, Eastgate Shopping Centre and a 24hour Tesco Extra. We're not far from the city centre and have two public bus stops just at the end of our road. We also have two bikes that our guests are welcome to use. If you're lucky, we can sometimes be around with our car to drop you where you need to be.
host_about:
Our Mum, Wendy, recently passed away in December 2017 after a short battle with an aggressive cancer. Mum worked as a Social Worker in the Adoption department and ran the AirBnB on the side, with the help of us; her three children (Ruby, Guy & Laurence) and her friends. Laurence named our home "The Wendy Estate" when Mum started sharing our home with AirBnB and various other lodgers she met & supported over the years. 

It was Mum's greatest wish that we continue to host our beloved cabin and treehouse on Airbnb and we hope to do so in a very 'Wendy like' fashion. 

Written by Wendy in 2015 ; "I am a Guardian reading, permaculture type, I work part time, love travelling, all things garden and 20th Century design. I like  sharing my lovely space with other people I am lucky to live in a rural oasis in the heart of a beautiful city which I know really well! "

A little bit about us... 

Ruby is the eldest & bossiest, she'll be making sure the rooms are up to scratch and there's enough tea and coffee in for you. Ruby is trained as a photographer but also knows all the best 'value for money' eateries & how to get about the city on public transport. 


Laurence is he's the music man of the three of us. He will tell you about the best forms of night life & the music culture of Bristol. 

Guy is the money making entrepreneur, he knows how to live a luxurious life and will give you ideas for how to have a truly luxurious time in Bristol.  

We all love food, music, and socialising. We live in a house full of books and many lovely items that make this house & the outbuildings our home and we look forward to continue sharing the 'Wendy Estate' with the rest of the world.

description:
Beautiful loft conversion in family home with own bathroom. Stunning panoramic views of Bristol from the front and peaceful gardens and allotments at the back.

We live on a quiet road 0.7 miles from Temple Meads train station and 1.4 miles from the city centre.

Continental breakfast provided for short term guests. Access to our shared kitchen can be arranged occasionally if needed.

neighborhood_overview:
We live in the Lower Knowle area of south Bristol. Our community is extremely friendly and on the border of Totterdown - a bohemian district of colourful, painted houses.

The city itself is a truly vibrant place, busy with cultural events and diverse communities. Bristol is full of historic sights from the Clifton Suspension bridge to the SS Great Britain and has a great reputation for street art (Banksy is from here), live music, festival culture, hot air balloons and world-class food.

As well as great shopping, theatre and cinemas nearby we’re also close to the beautiful open greenery of Ashton Court and fascinating Arnos Vale and in easy reach of the Mendips and Cotswolds.

Easy transport links to Bath, Wells, Bradford on Avon, Glastonbury, Clevedon, Weston Super Mare and Cheddar.

We are lucky enough to live within an easy walk or cycle of the city centre and harbour as well as Temple Meads so why not leave your car behind!

neighborhood_overview:
Elegant, leafy and filled with chic boutiques, cosy cafes, beautiful buildings and iconic attractions, such as Clifton Suspension Bridge and Bristol Zoo Gardens, Clifton is one of Bristol's most exclusive suburbs and picturesque quarters. Beginning with the Clifton Triangle and reaching into the area affectionately known as Clifton Village, this stunning Georgian area is always hugely popular with visitors.

The thriving hub of Clifton Village features pretty streets lined with boutiques and fine places to eat. name: The Robinson Building, converted Victorian factory
description:
The Robinson building is an old paper bag factory in the heart of Bristol which has been converted into bright and modern apartments. Featuring high ceilings and windows as well as thick brick walls you really feel as though you are living in a part of local history.

Situated in the vibrant Bedminster and Southville areas there is plenty to see and do on your doorstep and the center of town and harbourside are just a short walk away.
neighborhood_overview:
The Bedminster area is steeped in history and is a culturally vibrant hotspot. On the doorstep is East street which has convenience of common high street shops as well as a supermarket.

In the other direction is North Street with lots of independent shops, some stunning street art from Upfest (Europes largest street art festival) and Ashton Gate the home of Bristol City FC and Bristol Bears Rugby.

Whichever direction you head in there is also a cafe or pub to whet your whistle and it is only a short walk into town and the historic harbourside area, which is home to the SS Great Britain.

name: Contemporary Home in Friendly Easton, Free Parking
description:
We've just finished renovating our lovely home in Easton and would be delighted to host you while you explore Bristol.

With excellent transport links, both business and leisure travellers alike will be perfectly placed to get around. We have everything you could need to have a comfortable and enjoyable stay. Our house is handily located in a rare free parking zone!
neighborhood_overview: Excellent transport links, both business and leisure travellers alike will be perfectly placed to get around
host_about: We feel our place is an ideal base from which to explore this fabulous city. It’s a short hop to the city centre (ask for a three-stop hop on any local bus and you’ll be in Cabot Circus in no time). We have free on-street parking right outside our door, so you don’t have to worry about pay and display or the parking permits which now place restrictions on motorists in many other parts of the city. If you don’t have a car, that’s no problem, as there is a regular bus into town that stops on our street, or you can take the train from Stapleton Road station and be at Temple Meads or Clifton in no time. If you like a good walk, you can get to Broadmead in around 40 minutes by following the Bristol and Bath Railway Path into town. However, if you want to feel like a real Bristolian, the preferred way to get about Britain’s first ‘cycling city’ is by bike, of course. Our house is handily located next to the Bristol and Bath Railway Path, so why not bring your bikes? The ride to Bath through the Avon Valley is stunningI am a Bristolian born and raised; my wife and I met here at university. Bristol really is a beautiful city. We love taking walks around the Floating Harbour, ensuring we take time to stop for coffee at the Olive Shed, a swift half at the Nova Scotia Hotel, or maybe even a delicious bite to eat at the containers on Wapping Wharf. We also enjoy taking in the stunning views from the top of Brandon Hill before checking out the quirky, artsy shops on Park Street. We always like to look in at the Boston Tea Party on Park Street, where the ‘secret garden’ provides perfect respite from the hustle and bustle of the city. We’ve owned our house in Easton since July 2019. Recently voted one of the top 50 coolest neighbourhoods in the world by TimeOut Magazine (September 2019), Easton really does have something for everyone. You will find trendy cafés selling excellent coffee and home-made cakes, world-beating curry restaurants, and plenty of friendly local boozers. We like to visit the gorgeous Este Kitchen for coffee and brunch. Just opposite, the Greenbank pub is a great spot for lunch or an evening pint or two; their guest ales change all the time and they have a decent selection of board games. If you’re planning a quiet night in, G Bros Pizza will do you a perfectly baked pizza. The M’Sala Library truly is one of the best curries I’ve ever eaten; be sure to ask for the vegetable samosas which are to die for. For the discerning foodie, the famous Bristol Sweet Mart on St Mark’s Road is a five-minute walk away. There you’ll find ingredients for sale from all four corners of the globe. Worth a trip, even just for a browse. We look forward to hosting you soon in beautiful BS5. Chris, Justine and baby Louis.

neighborhood_overview:
Gloucester Road is a great street with many independent shops restaurants and cafes. 5 mins walk to park or county cricket and frequent buses to the centre and beyond. Stokes Croft is nearby with even more food and music.

This is the best part of Bristol.... it is rich with independent unusual and creative businesses of every sort. There is live music in several venues most nights, and great food inspired by the world, and by localism and seasonality. The shops are quirky, with fabulous gifts (some made locally) as well as essentials. Gloucester Road morphs into Stokes Croft- the artistic and creative hub of North Bristol- on its way to the centre with the river, and the SS Great Britain.
Bristol is a good base for touring about...it is near Bath, and not too far from Stonehenge and Longleat or the seaside at Weston Super Mare or Clevedon. It is also a good stopping off point if on a long journey from North to Southwest or from west Wales to the South East.

name: Harbourside heaven
description:
Mark and Corinne welcome you to Cumberland Road in Bristol’s historic harbour area.

This four bedroom semi detached Victorian house is on Spike Island, with the harbour to one side and the river the other.

The house is on four floors with big rooms and high ceilings. The garden looks over the harbour and also features a cabin with a double sofa bed.

Here you are just a few minutes’ walk from Bristol’s trendiest new quarter, Wapping Wharf - with two of the city’s highest rated restaurants.
neighborhood_overview:
This is the coolest place in the whole of Bristol. Ok so we are biased, but others think so too! The waterside vibe, the profusion of great places to eat and drink, the lack of roads to the rear and the location (very central) makes it unique.


Our recommendations for arts and culture:

- Arnolfini. A landmark arts centre and a beautiful spot on the harbour.

- Watershed. Just on the opposite quay, great for film.

- Bristol Museum. Usually has a good exhibition on but also has a great collection, particularly Victorian painters.

- Bristol Old Vic. Worth a visit as such a historic theatre and now looks fabulous after major refurb.

- Tobacco Factory. Very cool place, some good productions. Also on North Street, home to Upfest and some of the best graffiti in the country.

- M Shed. Tells the story of Bristol wonderfully.

- Banksy. Stuff everywhere, some iconic. There’s one by Bristol Marina near
host_about: Mark works for a conservation charity, Corinne is a sitting tribunal member and a criminologist at UWE.

name: Quiet spacious great location near Downs and town.
description:
Welcome to The Green room, it's the perfect place to explore what might just be the UK's coolest city. In a quiet side street in the East Clifton conservation area, you'll be in the heart of it all and at the same time feel a sense of space and closeness to nature, with the Downs nearby.
The accommodation is on the ground floor of our 3 storey, 1870 home. Imperfectly quirky, cosy and welcoming, we hope the green room will make you smile.
neighborhood_overview:
We think Bristol is the coolest place on earth and the Green Room, is brilliantly placed to explore it all from.

Close to home, the local area has cafes, restaurants and local shops for almost anything you could need. The Downs and the Botanic Gardens are on the doorstep.

A half hour walk can take you to the Centre and Harbourside, with their theatres, Waterside restaurants and bars, aquarium, We the Curious, M shed and the SS Great Britain.
Walk the same distance in a different direction and find yourself in the heart of alternative Bristol in Stokes Croft and the Gloucester Road, Europe's longest Street of independent shops.
Another direction again and a half hour's walk will take you to classy boho Clifton Village, with its cafes, antique shops, little independents and of course the world famous Suspension Bridge and visitor centre, Observatory and the Avon gorge.
The BBC, University and BRI are also close by.

description:
The garden house is a comfortable converted garage at the end of our garden. It is an open plan studio, heated by a pellet stove.

neighborhood_overview:
Windmill Hill is an eclectic, friendly and vibrant part of Bristol.
There is plenty to do and see in the local area: The City farm, The Harbourside, Wapping Wharf, The Malago river, Victoria Park, Perretts Park and North st shopping to name a few!

Annually there are some amazing events in the vicinity: Art on the Hill (The Arts trail) Balloon Fiesta and Upfest.

There are some good local pubs: The Victoria, The Distillery, The Rising Sun and The Brunel. Lots of great eateries too: Souk Kitchen, The Sundial, The Toast room, Yafo, The Lounge, The Tobacco factory, Mc Donald's, Acapella's and Florence pizzeria.

neighborhood_overview:
This beautiful studio apartment is tucked away on a quiet street in Clifton. Bristol is well-known for being a Georgian city with pretty architecture, and Clifton village is one of the city's most desirable locations. Within five minutes you can walk to a plethora of independent shops, cafes, pubs and restaurants as well as handy convenience stores such as Waitrose and Sainsbury's.

Clifton village is famous for its iconic Suspension Bridge, which stands out dramatically against the striking Avon Gorge. Straight over the bridge is Ashton Court Estate, a beautiful park spanning over 850 acres. There are numerous walking and cycling trails, as well as a Rose Garden, Deer Park and Mansion.

Some of our favourite spots in Clifton village include The White Lion rooftop bar, as well as The Fringe Jazz Bar, The Albion Pub, Bosco Pizzeria, Chandos Deli and East Village Cafe. You're also in a great spot to explore further afield: including Whiteladies Road, Park Street

Bristol is a charismatic city offering lots of its own food and culture to explore.
From the house, within easy walking distance is the Star pub, Gorilla Thai take-away, and supermarkets.

neighborhood_overview:
Welcome to Stokes Croft, the beating heart of Bristol's cultural and artistic scene! This vibrant neighborhood is bursting with creativity and energy, offering visitors a unique and eclectic experience that's unlike anything else in the city.

From colorful street art and live music performances to independent shops and trendy cafes, Stokes Croft has it all. Whether you're looking for a night out on the town or a quiet afternoon exploring local boutiques, you'll find plenty of options to suit your style and taste.

The community here is diverse and welcoming, with a strong sense of pride and camaraderie that's infectious. There's always something new to discover in Stokes Croft, whether it's a hidden gem of a restaurant or a pop-up art exhibit.

So come and experience the vibrant energy of Stokes Croft for yourself - you won't be disappointed!
host_about:

If you're renting the whole house you'll find full instructions on how the house works, and we can discuss whether you'd like me to get you a starter-pack of essential groceries.

host_about:

If you're renting a room for a night or so you'll be welcomed with a cup of tea, and possibly some baking if the writing's gone badly that day. You'll also meet the two happy terriers - or Not, if you're not keen on dogs. We'll agree what time you'd like breakfast, then I'll show you your room and how everything works, and leave you to yourselves. 
If you're renting the whole house you'll find full instructions on how the house works, and we can discuss whether you'd like me to get you a starter-pack of essential groceries. 
If you'd like a walk, you'll find a map of the local routes starting right from the garden gate. A selection of wellies by the back door. Plus details of the local pubs if you want to book an evening meal.

Within minutes, you can explore the lively Harbourside, home to museums, galleries, restaurants, and bars. Don’t miss M Shed for fascinating local history, the Arnolfini for contemporary art, and We The Curious for hands-on science fun. The iconic floating venue Thekla offers live music nights, while the Bristol Hippodrome, Bristol Beacon, O2 Academy, and the Old Vic provide top-class theatre, concerts, and performances.

neighborhood_overview:
Perched just south of Bristol’s city centre, Totterdown is a lively and creative neighbourhood known for its rainbow-painted houses, steep Victorian streets, and stunning city views. Popular with artists, young professionals, and families, it offers a welcoming community feel within walking distance of Temple Meads station, making it perfect for exploring Bristol and beyond.

Totterdown is packed with characterful pubs, independent cafés, and local eateries, while nearby Victoria Park and Perrett’s Park provide green spaces with panoramic views. The neighbourhood’s steep hills lead down to the buzzing harbourside, St. Nick’s Market, and Bristol’s cultural landmarks in just 15–20 minutes on foot.
